_readme: THIS FILE IS HAND-EDITED. Everything the promo site says lives here — copy, links, which
screenshots appear, how many feed items each panel shows. Edit it, commit, done.
feeds.json is the OTHER file, and it is generated by tools/feeds.mjs. Never edit that one:
a scheduled refresh overwrites it. The split is deliberate, so an automated feed pull can
never clobber the words on the page.
WRITE FOR A STRANGER. The first version of this file was written out of the design docs and
read like them: it said `nineteen named bands`, `deterministic`, `traced hulls` and `the
glyph original` before it ever said what you do with your hands. A word that only means
something to someone who has read the source is a word that costs a reader. Define a term
the first time it appears, or do not use it.
To point the CTA at a real Steam page, set cta.steam.url and the button stops saying soon.
notice.enabled false removes the banner above the summary entirely — no empty box, no gap.
soundings.json is a THIRD file and it is MACHINE-OWNED, appended to by a scheduled run.
The rules that run follows are in SOUNDINGS.md. Deleting an entry from soundings.json is
always safe — nothing reads back what it wrote, so a removed entry never comes back.
trailer.youtubeId is an ID, never a URL — site.js builds the embed itself and refuses
anything that is not eleven id characters. trailer.enabled false drops the whole section,
and the rail stop with it. NOTE the Short is NOT in the YouTube feed panel: the channel RSS
does not carry it, so this embed is the only way it appears on the page at all.
site.url is used for metadata only. The og: tags in index.html hold the SAME url and the
SAME description — link scrapers do not run JS, so they cannot read either from here. If
the site moves or the description changes, change both.

site.title: WHALE HOP — Lassen Seas
site.description: You are a whale with 150 seconds. Dive for speed, breach, flip, and land nose-first to keep the points. Climb from the trench floor to the top of the sky.
site.author: el3v8or

game.name: WHALE HOP
game.subtitle: LASSEN SEAS
game.tagline: a time-trial of flips, momentum & moonlight
game.blurb: You are a whale, and you have 150 seconds. Dive to build speed, breach, flip on the way up, and land nose-first to keep what you scored. Then do it again, higher. The trench floor is at −3,600m. The top of the sky is at 700,000m.
pitch: Points you score in the air are not yours yet. A clean entry banks them and hands back more speed than it took. A belly-flop loses the lot. That one rule is the whole game.
Land clean often enough and the heat gauge climbs — COLD, WARM, SIZZLING, BLAZING, SUPERNOVA. At the top, everything you touch is worth sixteen times as much.
Rails to grind, updrafts to ride, jet streams, anchor-stones that fling you, and rings that each buy you another second and a half. Speed is how you buy altitude, and everything good is higher up.

sections.heroFoot: THE CLIMB STARTS AT THE WATERLINE

gallery.heading: Nineteen bands, bottom to top
gallery.sub: A band is a stretch of sea or sky with its own colour, its own weather and its own things living in it. There are nineteen, and a good run passes through every one. Each frame below is a screenshot of the game actually running — nothing here is a mock-up.

soundings.heading: Notes from the water
soundings.sub: Short reports from somebody who is down there most days, half about the game and half about the actual ocean. A sounding is what you call a depth taken by dropping a weighted line — you learn how deep it is, not what lives there.

steam.label: WISHLIST ON STEAM
steam.note: There is no Steam page yet — it is still being built in the open. The devlog on Bluesky is where the date will turn up first.

features.title: Nothing you score in the air is yours yet
features.body: Every flip, grind and near-miss stacks up as a string of points you have not been paid for. Come down nose-first and the sea hands the whole string over — and returns more speed than it took, so a clean entry is really a launch. Come down flat and you keep half. Belly-flop and you lose the string, the heat and most of your momentum at once. Every other system in the game is a way of making that one bet more interesting.

features.title: Five tiers, and the top one is sixteen times
features.body: Clean entries feed a gauge that runs COLD → WARM → SIZZLING → BLAZING → SUPERNOVA, and every tier multiplies everything. The gap between a careful run and a hot one is not ten percent, it is a factor of sixteen. The gauge cools the entire time you are playing it safe, which is the point.

features.title: Five letters, five different ways to fly
features.body: W sits at the far end of a grind rail. H waits at the top of an updraft. A is down in the dark, L rides a jet stream, and E is higher than you have been yet. Each letter can only be reached by using a part of the game you would otherwise skip. Spell the word and the pot cashes out — and the pot is what you carry to the Fortune Table afterwards, where cards are dealt that haunt your next run only.

features.title: Pearls, cards, missions, and a casino at 300,000m
features.body: Score and altitude both pay pearls, and pearls buy 23 permanent upgrades — tail power, dive force, a wider near-miss aura, more moons hung higher in the sky. Change your mind and refund every one of them at full price, whenever you like. Under that sit 30 fortune cards, 22 long-haul missions, 8 relics unlocked by deed, and 12 modifiers that rewrite the rules outright. And at 300,000m the sky becomes THE ARCADE, where the house will gamble your entire run total if you ask it to.

features.title: One endless climb, and four built ones
features.body: DIVE is the main event: an endless, randomly assembled ascent you take as high as 150 seconds will carry you. LEVELS are hand-built instead, each with its own ocean, its own sky and its own list of demands. THE RISING follows a single hydrothermal plume from black-smoker vents on the trench floor to ice at the edge of space. SPUN SUGAR climbs the same distance as a sugar boil that breaks the surface as fizz. Finishing earns a medal — bronze is the floor, and the tiers are how well.

features.title: The whole ocean is made of typed characters
features.body: The sea, the sky, the starfield and the seabed are drawn out of monospace text — a hundred thousand small characters, drifting. The things you have to recognise instantly at speed, the whale and the fish and the rings and the satellites, are clean vector art laid over the top, sharing one near-black outline so the two layers read as a single world. It should look like an ocean somebody typed.

shots.caption: A built level breaking the surface. It starts on the trench floor among black-smoker vents and asks you for 10,000m.
Swim through a shoal and it falls in behind you. The fish hold your wake and copy every move you make, one at a time, right down the line — and they follow you out of the water.
The last altitude with weather in it. Above here the clouds run out and the sky starts going dark.
No horizon left to steer by. The strip down the left edge is the height map, and it is the only thing still telling you which way is up.
The ringed planet never appears below 15,000m. Seeing it at all means you got here.
A quarter of a million metres up, the sky goes faintly purple and the dark starts eating holes in the starfield.
Pure black, six loud colours and bumpers in every direction. The house is open, and it will take the whole run total off you.
